analysis:
The units are base-side text only (StandaloneServer.swift lines 1-1219). The only change is in the patch excerpt, at head lines ~1535-1564 in the memory-headroom wait loop. It adds a one-time `poolDropped` pass before LRU eviction. The pass calls the new `releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad()`, which awaits `GlobalKVCacheBudget.releaseRetainedKVSegments()` and then calls `MLX.Memory.clearCache()`, guarded by `nativeMiMoReclaimAllowed`.

Security view:
- This runs only in the standalone local-mode path, inside the load gate (`isLoadingAny`). It adds no new network surface, no auth change and no change to cache crypto, keys, TTL or HMAC lookup (T-041 is unaffected).
- Freeing retained KV segments and the MLX buffer pool before eviction avoids needless eviction and slightly lowers residual GPU-memory exposure (T-028). It does not widen it.
- The `continue` after the drop re-evaluates `availableMemoryGb()`, so the loop cannot spin. `poolDropped` is set before the await, so the drop runs at most once per call. `Task.checkCancellation` still runs on each iteration.
- `nativeMiMoReclaimAllowed` still gates `clearCache`, preserving the native MiMo ownership invariants.
- Open question: I could not see the implementations of `GlobalKVCacheBudget.releaseRetainedKVSegments()` or `busyEnginesKeepReclaimableMemory()`. The new clearCache could race with in-flight engines on other slots. That is a correctness/availability concern only, and no supplied evidence shows a security regression. The head-side bodies of the changed function are only partly visible in the patch, so a deeper pass over the GlobalKVCacheBudget changes (in another unit/file) would settle it.

No findings.
